Two weeks after the last vaccination, splenocytes were analyzed. The mRNA is comprised of a tandem minigene encoding three neoAgs (mCdt1, mScarb2 and mZfp106), including the epitope, identified from the murine gastric cancer YTN16 cell line [PMID 35008270].

immunization__comments: Mice were subcutaneously inoculated with 5 x 10^6 YTN16 cells on day 0, followed by vaccination and/or injection of anti-PD-1 antibody on days 7 and 14, or on days 10 and 17.  Mice were vaccinated twice with 5 μg of neoAg-mRNA-LNP or with 1 x 10^6 neoAg-dendritic cells (DCs) via subcutaneous injection, with a two-week interval between doses. The mRNA is comprised of a tandem minigene encoding three neoAgs (mCdt1, mScarb2 and mZfp106), including the epitope, identified from the murine gastric cancer YTN16 cell line [PMID 35008270]. Tumor growth was monitored every 2–3 days. On day 21, the tumors were harvested and analyzed using the MHC class I dimer assay.
assay__comments: Epitope-specific  CD8+ T cells were induced within the tumor and detected in all mice, including untreated ones, using MHC class I dimer staining. A greater number of neoAg-specific  CD8+ T cells infiltrated the tumor following neoAg-mRNA-LNP vaccination compared to neoAg-DC vaccination, and this effect was further intensified when combined with anti-PD-1 treatment.
